name: createScreenImage
signature: createScreenImage(QString id, QString filename, qreal x, qreal y, qreal scale=1.0, bool visible=true, qreal alpha=1.0, float fadeDuration=1.0)
description:
Creates and displays an image on the screen at the specified coordinates. The image is loaded from a file in the 'scripts/' directory and can be animated, moved, scaled, and faded. If an image with the same ID already exists, it will be deleted first.

IMPORTANT: The `scale` parameter affects the final resolution of the image! It is applied to the QPixmap BEFORE creating the graphics item. Using scale < 1 reduces resolution (saves memory but loses detail), while scale > 1 creates upsampling artifacts. For animations that grow/shrink an image, create at scale=1 and use setImageScale() for animated transitions.

If the file is not found, a qCWarning is emitted and NO image is created — the function does not throw or return an error.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the image (used to reference it later). If an image with this ID exists, it is deleted first.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Image file name, resolved via StelFileMgr with 'scripts/' prefix. Supports PNG, JPG, GIF, BMP.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: X-coordinate in pixels from the left edge of the screen

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Y-coordinate in pixels from the top edge of the screen

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Scale factor applied to the loaded pixmap (1.0 = original, 0.5 = 50%, 2.0 = double). Affects resolution permanently.

parameters.name: visible
parameters.description: Initial visibility state (true = visible at maxAlpha, false = hidden at opacity 0)

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: Maximum opacity when visible (0.0 = fully transparent, 1.0 = fully opaque)

parameters.name: fadeDuration
parameters.description: Fade duration in seconds for show/hide transitions. Fixed at creation — there is no scripting way to change it later.

compatibility.notes: fadeDuration is clamped to ≥ 0.001s internally. File lookup uses StelFileMgr with 'scripts/' prefix. If the file is missing, qCWarning(Scripting) is logged and no image is created.

name: getShowImage
description: Returns whether a screen image is currently visible (opacity > 0). Returns false if the image does not exist or is fully hidden.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the image

returnDescription: true if opacity > 0, false if hidden or not found

name: showImage
description: Shows or hides a screen image. The transition is animated over the image's fadeDuration (set at creation time via createScreenImage). When showing, opacity animates from current to maxAlpha; when hiding, from current to 0.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the image

parameters.name: show
parameters.description: true to fade in, false to fade out

compatibility.notes: Uses the fadeDuration set at creation. If the image is already in the target state, this is a no-op.

name: getImageWidth
description: Returns the width in pixels of the loaded QPixmap — i.e., the original image size AFTER the initial `scale` passed to createScreenImage. IMPORTANT: This does NOT reflect later setImageScale() calls (those change the graphics-item transformation, not the pixmap). To get the on-screen width, multiply this value by getImageScaleX().

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the image

returnDescription: Loaded pixmap width in pixels (after initial createScreenImage scale), or 0 if the image does not exist

compatibility.notes: Does NOT include setImageScale() transformations. Use getImageWidth() * getImageScaleX() for on-screen width.

name: getImageHeight
description: Returns the height in pixels of the loaded QPixmap — i.e., the original image size AFTER the initial `scale` passed to createScreenImage. IMPORTANT: This does NOT reflect later setImageScale() calls. To get the on-screen height, multiply by getImageScaleY().

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the image

returnDescription: Loaded pixmap height in pixels, or 0 if the image does not exist

name: getImageScaleX
description: Returns the TARGET horizontal scale factor of the image (the final value of the current scale animation), not the instantaneous scale during an animation. Returns 1.0 if setImageScale has never been called (the initial `scale` in createScreenImage is applied to the pixmap and does not affect this value).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the image

returnDescription: Target horizontal scale factor (1.0 = original loaded size), or 0 if image not found

compatibility.notes: Returns scaleAnim->horizontalScaleAt(1.) — the TARGET of the animation, not the current interpolated value. Returns 1.0 initially, even if createScreenImage was called with scale ≠ 1.

name: getImageScaleY
description: Returns the TARGET vertical scale factor of the image (the final value of the current scale animation), not the instantaneous scale during an animation. Returns 1.0 if setImageScale has never been called.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the image

returnDescription: Target vertical scale factor (1.0 = original loaded size), or 0 if image not found

compatibility.notes: Returns the target of the scale animation, not the current interpolated value.

example:
var sy = ScreenImageMgr.getImageScaleY("logo");
core.debug("Target vertical scale: " + sy);

name: setImageScale
signature: setImageScale(QString id, qreal scaleX, qreal scaleY, float duration=0.0)
description:
Sets the target scale of an image (relative to the loaded pixmap size), optionally animating the resize over a duration. This changes the QGraphicsItem transformation, NOT the underlying pixmap — getImageWidth()/getImageHeight() are unaffected. The pixmap is set to SmoothTransformation for the animation.

IMPORTANT: Even with duration=0, the animation runs for at least 0.001s (internally clamped) — 'instant' is not truly possible. For a snap change, use a very small duration like 0.001.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the image

parameters.name: scaleX
parameters.description: Target horizontal scale factor relative to loaded size (1.0 = original, >1 = enlarge, <1 = shrink)

parameters.name: scaleY
parameters.description: Target vertical scale factor relative to loaded size

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Animation duration in seconds. Internally clamped to ≥ 0.001s — 'instant' is not possible.

compatibility.notes: Uses QGraphicsItemAnimation with SmoothTransformation. Clamps duration to ≥ 0.001s. getImageScaleX/Y return the TARGET immediately, not the current value.

name: setImageAlpha
description:
Sets the maximum opacity (alpha) of a screen image. This value determines the opacity when the image is fully visible. The change is applied INSTANTLY — the fade animation is stopped and the new opacity is set immediately. The fadeDuration only affects show/hide transitions via showImage(), not alpha changes.

Values: 0.0 = fully transparent, 1.0 = fully opaque.

NOTE: The .hpp documentation for the underlying C++ method has the values inverted (it says 1.0=transparent, 0.0=opaque), but the actual implementation follows Qt's setOpacity: 0=transparent, 1=opaque. This documentation follows the actual behavior.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the image

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: New maximum opacity (0.0 = fully transparent, 1.0 = fully opaque)

compatibility.notes: Applied instantly (fadeTimer is stopped). Only effective when the image is currently visible (getShowImage() returns true) — if hidden, maxAlpha is stored and applied on next showImage(true).

name: setImageXY
signature: setImageXY(QString id, qreal x, qreal y, float duration=0.0)
description: Moves an image to a specific screen position. Coordinates are measured in pixels from the top-left corner. With duration=0 (default) the move is instant; with duration>0 the movement is animated linearly over the given time.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the image

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: New X-coordinate in pixels from the left edge

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: New Y-coordinate in pixels from the top edge

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Animation duration in seconds (0 = instant, default 0)

compatibility.notes: Uses QTimeLine with linear easing. Duration=0 is truly instant (no clamping). If the target position equals the current position, the call is a no-op.

name: addImageXY
signature: addImageXY(QString id, qreal x, qreal y, float duration=0.0)
description:
Moves an image by adding offsets to its current position. Equivalent to setImageXY(currentX + x, currentY + y, duration). Useful for relative movements without needing to track absolute positions.

NOTE: If called during an ongoing setImageXY animation, the offset is applied to the CURRENT instantaneous position (tex->pos()), not the target. This may lead to cumulative drift if called rapidly during an animation.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the image

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: X offset in pixels (positive = right, negative = left)

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Y offset in pixels (positive = down, negative = up)

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Animation duration in seconds (0 = instant)

compatibility.notes: Internally calls setXY(currentPos + offset). During an ongoing animation, currentPos is the instantaneous position, not the target.

name: deleteImage
description: Permanently removes a screen image from memory. The image will no longer be displayed or accessible. Any pending animations are stopped and all QTimeLine/QGraphicsItemAnimation objects are deleted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the image to delete

compatibility.notes: No-op if the ID does not exist (no exception, no warning).

name: deleteAllImages
description: Removes all screen images from memory. Useful for cleanup at the end of a presentation or before loading a new set of images.

compatibility.notes: Does not save anything (no immediateSave). After this call, getAllImageIDs() returns an empty list.

name: getAllImageIDs
description: Returns a list of all currently loaded image identifiers, sorted alphabetically (QMap key order). Useful for iterating, existence checks, or debugging.
returnDescription: Alphabetically sorted list of image IDs (empty if no images loaded)

compatibility.notes: QMap::keys() returns keys in sorted order (by QString locale-independent comparison).
